⛽ Petrol is back to 161.3p a litre — the highest since November 2022, according to the ONS.

Diesel jumped 14.2p in a SINGLE MONTH to 181.8p. Motor fuel inflation is running at 23.0%.

Four years ago, numbers like these led the news for a fortnight. This time? A sub-heading. 🤔

Here's my honest read on why.

If you live near a mainline station, a 9p rise is an irritation. If you're a carer driving between visits, a sole trader with a van, a nurse on shifts no bus timetable covers, or anyone in rural Lancashire — it's a pay cut. One that arrives with no letter, no vote, and nobody to complain to. 🚗

And diesel at 181.8p doesn't stay at the pump. It rides into the price of everything that arrives on a lorry. You'll meet it again on a shelf. 🛒

No government controls the world oil market. But they do control fuel duty, how exposed we are to imported energy, and who carries the hit.
